vael_intro.title: Air
vael_intro.narrator: Vael. Bearer of Air. What he avoids saying.
vael_intro.text:
The problem with air
is that you only notice it when it's missing.

Or when it shoves someone into a fountain.

I should clarify right away:
the fountain was already there.

Technically,
all I did was introduce two elements.

Water.

And the merchant who was shouting too loudly.

vael_pourquoi_air.title: Why Air
vael_pourquoi_air.text:
Air owns nothing.

It passes.
It touches.
It moves on.

It's convenient.

When you stay somewhere too long,
people start asking questions.

**"Where are you from?"**
**"Why are you smiling like that?"**
**"Was it you who hung the provost's underwear from the belfry?"**

Yes.

But that's not the point.

The point is that air knows how to get in anywhere
without asking permission.

And how to leave before anyone asks it to account for itself.

vael_fuite.title: A Very Elegant Escape
vael_fuite.text:
Running away is a harsh word.

I prefer:
strategic repositioning with panache.

But yes.

Maybe.

When I was a child,
I already knew how to vanish from a room
before anyone got angry.

Which was useful,
since I was often the reason
for that anger.

My father used to say:

**"Vael, one day your humor is going to kill you."**

I answered:

**"Then I hope it does it fast,**
**because I can't stand long speeches."**

He didn't laugh.

My mother did.

Quietly.

Quiet victories matter, you know.

vael_enfance.title: The Rooftops
vael_enfance.text:
I was born in a town where the streets climbed more than they went anywhere.

The houses were packed together.
The balconies too close.
The roof tiles nearly polished by the children who ran across them.

Well.

By me.

The other children had more respect for gravity.

A failing of character.

My mother was a messenger.
My father repaired weather vanes, bells, and anything hung far too high
for sensible people.

He used to say:

**"If you fall, shout before you hit the ground."**

A strange piece of advice.

Very useful, later on.

vael_mere.title: The Messenger
vael_mere.text:
My mother knew the whole town.

Not the streets.

The shortcuts.

The difference is huge.

A street takes you where everyone goes.
A shortcut takes you where no one is waiting for you.

She taught me to listen to doors,
to footsteps,
to badly closed windows,
to silences that last one second too long.

**"People talk even when they're silent."** she used to say.

I listened.

Then I repeated things at the wrong moment.

That's how you learn diplomacy.

Or how you get chased by a baker.

The two are more alike than you'd think.

vael_premiere_chute.title: The First Fall
vael_premiere_chute.location: Upper Town — Roof of the old mill
vael_premiere_chute.text:
I was seven.

I was running across the roof of the old mill.

Forbidden.
Dangerous.
Great fun.

It was drizzling a little.

Not enough to stop.
Just enough to make a child already fully committed to that direction
a bit more reckless.

My foot slipped.

I tipped over.

The world spun.
The sky slid beneath me.
The town above.

I screamed.

Not from fear.

Because my father had told me to.

And the air caught me.

choices.text: What do you mean, caught you?

vael_air_rattrape.title: Caught
vael_air_rattrape.text:
Not like arms.

More like a very firm idea
deciding the ground could wait.

I hung there.

Upside down.
Arms open.
One shoe gone.

An old woman looked at me from her window.

**"You again?"**

I said:

**"Technically, I'm not really *here* anymore."**

She shut her shutters.

The air set me down gently in a cart full of laundry.

White.
Clean.

Not for long.

vael_peur_chute.title: Afraid?
vael_peur_chute.location: Upper Town — Between sky and ground
vael_peur_chute.text:
Yes.

Obviously.

I'm funny,
not reckless.

Well.

Not entirely.

The fear came first in my stomach.
Then in my throat.
Then in my hands.

And just before the ground,
it turned into something else.

An opening.

As if the world were saying:

*You can fall.*

*Or you can go somewhere else.*

I chose somewhere else.

I often choose somewhere else.

vael_reaction_parents.title: The Parents
vael_reaction_parents.text:
My mother laughed.

Not right away.

First she checked my arms,
my legs,
my head.

Mostly my head.

**"She was already like this before."** my father said.

Then she laughed.

My father didn't laugh.

He looked at the open window.
The curtains moving without any wind.
Me, covered in damp laundry.

**"You called out."**

**"I shouted."**

**"And something answered."**

It was the first time I'd seen my father serious
without being angry.

I didn't like it.

So I made a joke.

Bad idea.

As usual.

vael_mauvaise_blague.title: A Bad Idea
vael_mauvaise_blague.text:
I said:

**"At least now we know I fall with style."**

Silence.

Long.

My father closed his eyes.

My mother stared at the ceiling.

I think she was praying.

Not for my survival.

For her patience.

Then my father said:

**"You must not show that."**

And then
the room grew smaller.

The windows too.

Even the air seemed hesitant to come in.

vael_apprendre.title: Learning to Pass
vael_apprendre.text:
I learned on my own.

Well, on my own with the air.

Which is a sentence normal people avoid saying.

Every morning I threw feathers from the rooftops.
I tried to make them spin.
Then rise.
Then slip through an open window.

One day I succeeded.

Into a soup.

At the provost's.

I won't pretend it wasn't intentional.
That would be beneath both of us.

I learned that air doesn't force.

It goes around.
It lifts.
It diverts.
It pushes just enough that things almost choose for themselves.

vael_limites.title: Limits
vael_limites.text:
The limit of air
is that it can't hold on to anything for long.

A stone,
you can set down.

A flame,
you can feed.

Water,
you can collect.

Air?

Air slips away.

So do I.

I could slow a fall.
Turn an arrow aside.
Carry a whisper from one room to another.

But if I tried to keep something too long,
my hands would shake.
My breath would catch.

As if the world were reminding me:

*What passes was not made to stay.*

A beautiful line.

Very annoying when you want to keep someone.

vael_recrutement.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
vael_recrutement.text:
He arrived one evening.

Well.

Arrived.

I mostly noticed because he was already sitting next to me
on the belfry roof.

Which is rude.

Roofs have etiquette.
You don't just appear on people's roofs.

He wore white and gray.
His hair moved though there was no wind.

Showoff.

**"Did you sense me coming?"**

**"No."**

**"Good."**

**"I find that debatable."**

He smiled.

**"You're Vael."**

**"Depends who's asking."**

vael_esprit_air.title: The Spirit of Air
vael_esprit_air.text:
His name was Eolan.

Or so he said.

With air,
you always keep a small margin of suspicion.

He explained the Order to me.
The Five Blades.
Chaos.
The prophecy.
The spirits.

A lot of information for a rooftop.

I asked:

**"And if I refuse?"**

He looked out over the town.

**"Then you stay."**

**"That's it?"**

**"Yes."**

That worried me.

People who really let you choose
are far more dangerous than those who give orders.

vael_depart.title: Departure
vael_depart.text:
My parents listened.

My father standing.
My mother seated.
Me on the windowsill,
which didn't help the mood.

**"Come down from there."** said my father.

**"Symbolically or physically?"**

**"Vael."**

I came down.

Eolan spoke softly.

At the end,
my mother gave me her old messenger's satchel.

**"Shortcuts are no use**
**if you forget where you wanted to go."**

My father gave me a small broken weather vane.

**"So you know where the wind is coming from."**

I said:

**"Am I supposed to be touched or insulted?"**

He held me close.

Touched, then.

vael_aurenthal.title: Aurenthal
vael_aurenthal.text:
Aurenthal was enormous.

Which is a polite way of saying:
far too sure of itself.

The Temple too.

Tall columns.
Solemn silence.
Statues that look at you as if they'd paid the entrance fee.

Three children were waiting.

A girl with silver hair.
Very calm.
Too calm.
Very calm people always hide either great wisdom
or a desire to hit someone with a chair.

A boy who looked like an argument standing up.

And a girl who smiled as if she had decided everyone deserved a chance.

I thought:

*She's brave.*

Or badly informed.

vael_ikar_debut.title: Ikar — Bad Weather
vael_ikar_debut.text:
Ikar didn't greet me.

He looked at me.

The way you look at a squeaky door.

I said:

**"Charmed, I'm sure."**

He didn't answer.

On the third day,
I made his blade vanish during training.

A small disappearance.
Very temporary.
Almost educational.

He set the ground on fire.

**"Very funny."**

**"I wanted to see if you'd panic."**

**"And?"**

**"You turned the courtyard into toast."**
**"So yes, but with style."**

He almost smiled.

Almost.

I counted it as a military victory.

vael_aryn_debut.title: Aryn — Too Calm
vael_aryn_debut.text:
Aryn spoke little.

Which immediately struck me as suspicious.

Not because she was hiding something.

Because she really listened.

People who really listen are terrible.
They hear the things we haven't said.

One evening she asked me:

**"Do you always joke when you're scared?"**

I answered:

**"No. Sometimes I joke when other people are scared."**

She looked at me.

For a long time.

**"So yes."**

I hated that.

I came to respect her a great deal afterward.

vael_entrainement.title: Training
vael_entrainement.text:
Eolan rarely trained me on the ground.

**"The ground breeds bad habits."**

A typical line from someone who never had to scrub their own boots.

He made me run across the Temple's rooftops.
Leap between towers.
Eavesdrop on conversations through three walls.
Catch a leaf before it touched the water.

Then he would vanish.

In the middle of a sentence.

The first time, I shouted:

**"That's very rude!"**

His voice answered from behind me:

**"That's very efficient."**

I liked him.

It was unbearable.

choices.text: Did he talk to you about the others?

vael_eolan_autres.title: Eolan and the Others
vael_eolan_autres.text:
Eolan said the others were easy to read.

Which was false.

But he said a lot of false things
to see whether I would correct them.

**"Fire moves forward."**

**"Right up to the wall."**

**"Water flows around."**

**"And ends up in your boots."**

**"Earth stays put."**

I didn't reply to that.

He smiled.

**"And air?"**

I shrugged.

**"Air pretends to leave."**

Eolan looked far into the distance.

**"Yes."**

It was the first time he looked sad.

Only briefly.

Like a draft you thought you'd invented.

vael_pret_a_tout.title: Ready for Anything
vael_pret_a_tout.location: Temple of the Order — East tower
vael_pret_a_tout.text:
I was ten when Eolan said the line.

The big one.
The famous one.
Very handy when you want to traumatize children with elegance.

**"The bearer of Chaos will come."**

**"Could he at least warn us first?"**

**"Vael."**

**"Sorry. Go on. I'm interrupting the prophecy."**

He didn't laugh.

Bad sign.

**"You must be ready for anything."**

I looked at the void below the tower.

The wind was rising.

**"'Anything' is a very broad word."**

**"Yes."**

**"Handy for not explaining a thing."**

He didn't answer.

So I understood I was right.

vael_compris_tout.title: What I Understood
vael_compris_tout.location: Temple of the Order — East tower
vael_compris_tout.text:
I understood that nobody really knew.

Not entirely.

The spirits had seen Caël.
They had seen what fear had made of him.

And instead of giving us an answer,
they gave us a sentence.

*Ready for anything.*

Ikar heard:
*strike if necessary.*

Taera heard:
*never give up.*

Aryn heard:
*keep searching.*

Me?

I heard the silence around the word *anything*.

What we don't say is sometimes louder
than what we shout.

vael_blague_tout.title: The Joke
vael_blague_tout.location: Temple of the Order — East tower
vael_blague_tout.text:
I said:

**"Ready for anything, even the boiled vegetables from the refectory?"**

Eolan looked at me.

**"Especially those."**

I laughed.

A real laugh.

Then he added:

**"One day you'll joke in front of someone who thinks you're mocking their pain."**

I stopped.

**"I don't do that."**

**"Not on purpose."**

The wind turned cold.

I wasn't hungry anymore.

Not even to complain about the vegetables.

Tells you something.

vael_annees.title: The Years
vael_annees.location: Temple of the Order — Everywhere except where they were looking for me
vael_annees.text:
We grew up.

Aryn grew quieter,
which seemed impossible and yet.

Ikar got better with a blade,
and worse at conversation.

Taera made things grow in every spare corner.
One day she planted mint beside my window.

**"So it smells nice."**

**"Did I smell bad?"**

**"No."**

Pause.

**"Your room, maybe."**

Betrayal.

I traveled a lot inside the Temple.
The corridors.
The roofs.
The archives.
The forbidden places.

Especially the forbidden places.

They're always better ventilated.

vael_archives.title: The Archives
vael_archives.location: Temple of the Order — Forbidden archives
vael_archives.text:
I didn't go into the forbidden archives.

It's important to make that clear.

I passed through them.

The difference is legal.

One evening I found Aryn there.
She was reading an old account about Caël.

**"You shouldn't be here."** she said.

**"Neither should you."**

**"I'm looking for something."**

**"So am I."**

**"What?"**

I glanced at the shelves.

**"A way out, now that you've seen me."**

She almost smiled.

Then she showed me the text.

The former Taera had reached out a hand to Caël.

And for a moment,
it had worked.

vael_quinze_ans.title: Fifteen
vael_quinze_ans.text:
At fifteen,
I was officially unbearable.

Unofficially too.

But I was useful.

I could hear a conversation from the far end of a courtyard.
I could knock a sword out of someone's hand without touching their arm.
I could vanish down a straight corridor,
which annoys methodical people no end.

Ikar, then.

But most of all,
I knew when someone was lying while laughing.

It's very precise.

Aryn rarely lied.
Taera never very well.
Ikar lied like a burning door.

Me?

I was excellent.

That's why I was quick to catch myself out.

vael_mensonge.title: The Lie
vael_mensonge.location: Temple of the Order — North roof
vael_mensonge.text:
I joked when I was scared.

I joked when others suffered,
not to deny their pain,
but to leave them a step to put their foot on.

A tiny step.

Sometimes it worked.

Sometimes not.

The trouble
was that I had started using that step for myself too.

After a while,
I no longer knew whether I was making others laugh
or covering the sound of something falling apart inside me.

I could have talked about it.

To Aryn.
To Taera.
Even to Ikar, if I'd planned on armor first.

I didn't.

I made a joke.

Classic.

vael_nuit_signal.title: The Signal
vael_nuit_signal.location: Temple of the Order — Temple roof
vael_nuit_signal.text:
The night the Chaos woke,
the wind stopped.

Completely.

Do you know what's worse than a storm?

The absence of wind.

Because then
even the air holds its breath.

I was on the Temple roof.
Naturally.

My blade vanished from its scabbard.

Then it came back.

Then it vanished again.

**"Very mature."** I said.

It came back into my hand.

Cold.
Light.
Uneasy.

I didn't know a sword could be uneasy.

Mine had always had plenty of personality.

vael_sentir_chaos.title: What I Felt
vael_sentir_chaos.text:
Not anger.

Not only.

The Chaos made noise,
but in the middle of it there was an emptiness.

Like someone calling out
without knowing which name to say.

I thought of Caël.

Of the prophecy.
Of all the people who had been afraid of him
before even knowing him.

Then I thought:

*He's alone.*

And right after:

*That, I know.*

The wind came back.

Just enough to push me toward the stairs.

Very subtle.

For an invisible kick.

vael_reveiller_autres.title: Waking the Others
vael_reveiller_autres.text:
I went to wake the others.

Well.

Tried to.

Aryn was already up.
Taera too.
Ikar was already wearing his armor.

Very annoying.

It was as if I were late for my own alarm.

**"I had prepared a dramatic entrance."**

**"Not now."** said Ikar.

**"It's always now for a dramatic entrance."**

Aryn looked at me.

That look meant:
*Vael.*

Not my name.

The whole concept.

I raised my hands.

**"Fine. Bad timing."**

Then I added:

**"But excellent narrative tension."**

Taera smiled.

A little.

That was enough.

vael_ikar_nuit.title: Ikar That Night
vael_ikar_nuit.text:
Ikar had that face.

The face of people who have already decided
and hope someone will stop them
without making them ask.

I saw it at once.

I pretended not to see anything.

That's my talent.

But in the courtyard, before we left,
I caught up with him.

**"Ikar."**

**"What."**

**"You don't have to carry that alone."**

He said nothing.

**"There are four of us."** I added.
**"Five soon."**
**"The weight gets divided."**

He looked at me.

Not the look he usually gives me.
Not *"what do you want now"*.

Something else.

He nodded.

Then he walked back to his horse.

He slowed down a little.

Just a little.

vael_depart_temple.title: Departure
vael_depart_temple.text:
Four silhouettes in the courtyard.

Aryn calm.
Taera steady.
Ikar on fire, even when he wasn't burning.

Me,
trying not to whistle.

I lasted thirty seconds.

Eolan appeared one last time.

He wasn't there.
That's important to point out.

But he wasn't there in a very present way.

He looked at me.

**"You know what to do."**

**"I mostly know what not to do."**

**"Often it's the same thing."**

He vanished.

I whistled a little.

Not on purpose.

Ikar sighed.

A good start to the journey.

choices.text: Look back at the Temple one last time.

vael_route.title: The Road
vael_route.text:
The road was long.

So I whistled.

The road was unsettling.

So I whistled better.

Ikar hated it.
Which proved I still had a positive influence on the world.

Halfway there,
I caught up with him.

**"You don't have to carry that alone."**

He said he wasn't carrying anything.

Of course.

Aryn didn't speak.
Taera sometimes touched the ground from her horse.

I listened to the wind.

It came from the east.
From Cendral.

It smelled of ash.

And of something else.

Someone who had just lost everyone
and was still breathing.

vael_pensee_joueur.title: The Player
vael_pensee_joueur.text:
I didn't know him yet.

The bearer of Chaos.

The boy from the prophecy.
The walking catastrophe.
The future end of the world, according to people who were probably selling charms against misfortune in front of the Temple.

I didn't know him.

But I already knew one thing.

Everyone was going to look at him as an answer.

A yes.
A no.
A threat.
A miracle.
A weapon.
A mistake.

Nobody likes being reduced to a single word.

People had often reduced me to a joke.

It's lighter.

But it still weighs something.

vael_fumee.title: The Smoke
vael_fumee.text:
We saw the smoke.

Black.
Thick.
Very dramatic.

Frankly,
if the prophecy had hired a set designer,
it couldn't have done better.

I didn't say that.

Because Vael, nineteen,
sometimes carries traces of accidental wisdom.

My blade vanished.

Then it came back into my hand.

Aryn closed her eyes.

**"He's still there."**

Taera placed her hand on the ground.

**"He's alive."**

Ikar looked at the smoke.
For a long time.

He said nothing.

So, for once,
I didn't say anything either.

The wind came from Cendral.

It trembled.

vael_derniere_pensee.title: The Last Thought
vael_derniere_pensee.text:
My mother used to say shortcuts are no use
if you forget where you wanted to go.

My father used to say you have to shout before you hit the ground.

Eolan said many things,
then vanished before anyone could ask him to clarify.

Very handy.
Very cowardly.
Very air.

Looking at the smoke,
I understood one simple thing.

The boy over there was falling.

Everyone was going to tell him what to do.

Stop.
Control.
Come back.
Don't destroy.
Don't become that.
Don't become him.

Maybe what he really needed
was to hear someone shout with him.

Just before the ground.

fin_memoire_vael.title: Ending — Vael's Memory
fin_memoire_vael.text:
Memory passes.

Like air — without a sound, leaving no visible trace.

vael_fuite_detail.title: What It Really Was
vael_fuite_detail.text:
It was several things.

First, the questions.

The villagers asked a lot of questions.
*What are you going to do next?*
*Do you look like your father or your mother?*
*Are you going to stay here your whole life?*

I didn't have the answers.

So I left.

Up on the roofs.
Nobody asked questions up there.

The air didn't ask anything either.

It simply accepted that you were there.

That was enough.

vael_mere_ressemble.title: The Resemblance
vael_mere_ressemble.text:
Everyone says so.

The same way of looking sideways.
The same way of answering off the point.
The same way of vanishing before anyone notices.

She found it funny.

**"Will you be a messenger too?"**

**"I'll deliver the air."**

**"Air doesn't get delivered."**

**"Exactly."**

She had laughed.

My mother laughed with her whole body.

People who laugh with their whole body
aren't afraid of anything.

Or they've learned to pretend
better than anyone.

I never found out which.

vael_eolan_phrase.title: The Great Line
vael_eolan_phrase.text:
Eolan used to say things like:

**"Air is everywhere and nowhere."**

**"Very handy."** I would answer.

**"Air sees everything without being seen."**

**"Even handier."**

**"Air..."**

**"Eolan."**

**"What."**

**"Just say what you mean."**

He fell silent.

Then:

**"Air understands people better than people understand each other."**
**"Because it hears them think."**

**"There you go."** I said.
**"That wasn't so hard."**

He vanished.

I think I'd annoyed him.

We got along well.

vael_taera_debut.title: Taera — The Garden
vael_taera_debut.text:
Taera had a garden.

In the inner courtyard.

I couldn't see the point.

**"What's the use?"**

**"It grows."**

**"And so?"**

She looked at me.

**"Have you never watched something grow?"**

**"No."**

**"Sit down."**

I sat down.

We watched.

Twenty minutes.

Nothing.

**"It's not growing fast."**

**"No."**

**"Is that the point?"**

**"It's one of the points."**

I didn't understand.

I came back the next day all the same.

And the day after that.

There was nothing to do.
Just be there.

It was restful.

vael_dernier_regard.title: The Last Look
vael_dernier_regard.text:
I hadn't planned to do it.

But as we left, I looked up.

The tall columns.
The solemn silence.

Twelve years.

No need to count the memories —
they come on their own if you look long enough.

The first day in the refectory.
Ikar folding his arms.
Aryn looking at her hands.
Taera smiling at everyone.

And me, who had made my own plate vanish by accident.

We had all looked surprised.

It was the beginning of something.

I lowered my eyes.

**"Coming?"** said Aryn.

**"I was looking at the clouds."**

She knew I was lying.

She said nothing.

That's why we get along.

vael_reconnait_vide.title: The Emptiness Recognized
vael_reconnait_vide.text:
Yes.

Because I had the same kind.

Not the same size.
Not the same sort.

But that moment when you search
for something to hold on to
and find nothing.

The prophecy.
The Chaos.
Destiny.

Big words.

But underneath there was just someone
who had wanted to help
and had broken everything.

I knew what that was.

Not the Chaos.

Shame.

And shame with no one to say
*it's not your fault* —

it turns into something else.

Something much more dangerous.

vael_cri.title: The Shout
vael_cri.text:
I hadn't shouted yet.

Hadn't found what to shout.

My father had shouted *watch out.*

Handy, but not very inspired.

My mother had shouted *ah* very loudly
and the vase changed direction.

I was still searching.

Something useful.
Something true.
Something that resembles what I actually wanted to say.

We'd see.

The smoke was there.

I hadn't shouted yet.

But for the first time in a long while —

I really had something to say.
